doc.title: Bley Carla — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: First piano lessons, singing and biting her mother
summary: She learned piano from both parents, played at church events, sang at three with a tin cup, and her mother stopped teaching after she bit her.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Ok. So you, there’s, I had in my research, looked at or gone through some of the prior interviews, and of course one particular one with Ben Sidran, that talked about your pre-teen days. And also looking at your inclination for music. And, tell us about that, ‘cause this is something that I think is very interesting to see at a young age that you already had the passion, or at least an interest in it.
Well my father was a piano teacher, so I learned to play as I learned to walk, you know. It’s just so natural. My mother was also a musician, and gave me piano lessons.
So I had piano lessons from a very early age from two people, my parents.
And I thought I was a great pianist, but I found out later that I wasn’t. But before I found it out I played at all the church things, like you know, Youth for Christ. I forget
some of the names. And, umm, the church was my life until I was twelve or thirteen. Then I discovered the rest of the world.
In this interview with Ben there was this conversation about your singing also?
Oh yeah, that was my first recital as a singer.
I was maybe, I don’t know, three. And I sang This Little Light of Mine, and held out a tin cup, and people put money in it. But I had to give it to my parents.
Ahh, ok. So, umm, you said your mother also taught you piano.
What was some of the literature or what were they teaching there?

I mean very, very simple. My father taught people who could hardly play, you know. Early students. I don’t know if I’ve told anyone this yet, but my mother taught me until I bit her when she made me get the right fingering. And she never taught me again, and she gave me to my father, who I never bit.
[Laughs] I’ve heard of the opposite where the teacher has a ruler and smacks you on the hand, but never heard of the student biting the teachers, so that’s one for the books there.
